transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time with this. Um, I guess the main reason I'm here is... well, I'm a registered nurse, and lately, I've just been having a little trouble staying focused on the floor. It's probably nothing major, just, you know, normal stress maybe? 

But, um, I find myself losing my train of thought a lot. Like, if an IV pump beeps down the hall, or if someone asks another nurse a question, or a call light goes off... I just get a bit sidetracked. And then suddenly I realize I've completely forgotten what patient flow issue I was working on. It's a little embarrassing to admit, honestly. I just want to make sure I'm doing my best for my patients, you know? Does that make sense?
Did you have this same kind of trouble staying focused when you were a child?

Well, um... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I think a lot of kids get distracted, right? But, um, looking back, even in elementary school, my teachers would always write on my report cards that I was a bright girl, which was nice of them, but... they'd also say I was a bit careless. 

I was always losing my worksheets or, you know, just forgetting to turn in my homework even if I had actually done it. It wasn't because I didn't care! I really wanted to do well. But my mom, bless her, she actually had to sit with me at the kitchen table every single night just to keep me on track with my assignments. I feel bad she had to do that, honestly. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Outside of work, do these focus problems cause trouble in your daily life?

Um, well... I mean, I try really hard to keep everything together, I really do. But, um, I guess I do have some slip-ups at home, too. It's probably just because I'm so tired from work, right? But... I do tend to forget things that should be, you know, just normal, routine stuff. 

Like, I'll completely forget to call my mom back, or I'll miss paying a bill on time... or even just showing up for a dentist appointment. And the worst part is, I really meant to do it! Sometimes I even set a reminder on my phone, and it just... slips right out of my head anyway. It's so silly of me, I know I should be better organized. I hope that doesn't sound too irresponsible? I really am trying my best to stay on top of things.
Do you often find yourself worrying a lot, even when there isn’t an immediate problem?

Oh, um... worrying? I mean, I guess I have normal worries, like anyone else, right? Just, you know, wanting to do a good job at the hospital and making sure my patients are okay. But I wouldn't say I sit around agonizing over things when everything is fine. 

I really try to stay positive and not let things get to me too much. I mean, as a nurse, you kind of have to keep a level head, so I do my best to just focus on what's in front of me. I hope that's the right answer? I just... I don't think I'm an overly anxious person, if that's what you're asking. Does that make sense?
Do you often put off tasks that require a lot of sustained mental effort, like paperwork or charting?

Well, um... I guess I might do that sometimes? But I really think it's just because I want to be a good nurse, you know? Like, I always want to be there for my patients first. 

But, um... if I know a task is going to take a lot of focused chart review—like if I have to audit documentation across different shifts—I might... kind of push it off? I'll usually go find bedside tasks to do instead, just because sitting down with all that paperwork feels... I don't know, almost like trying to climb a wall? It just feels so overwhelming. But I always make sure my patients are taken care of! I really hope you don't think I'm just being lazy about the charting... I do try to get to it eventually. Is that normal for someone in my line of work?
Do you often feel restless, like it’s hard to sit still?

Oh, um... restless? Like, physically? No, I don't think so. I mean, I can sit still just fine if I need to. 

I guess I do like to stay busy, you know? Being on my feet a lot is just part of being a nurse, and I actually really enjoy that part of it. It feels good to be moving around the unit and checking on people. But I wouldn't say I feel... driven by a motor or anything like that. When I finally get home and get to sit on the couch, I'm usually perfectly happy to just stay there. 

I'm not fidgety or bouncing off the walls, I promise. I hope that's okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how things are.
Do you often have trouble falling asleep or staying asleep?

Oh, um... sleep? No, I don't think I have any real trouble with that. I mean, I sleep pretty well, honestly. 

Sometimes it takes me a little bit to wind down after a long shift, but I think that's just because nursing can be so demanding, right? Your brain is just kind of reviewing the day. But once I'm asleep, I'm usually out for the night. I really try to practice good sleep hygiene and make sure I'm rested for my patients the next day. 

I definitely don't lie awake for hours or anything. I hope that's what you were looking for? I just want to be helpful.
